_description: Machining DFM rules (drilling, milling, turning). Boolean fields use 1 = true and 0 = false. Part-level variables (e.g. min_tool_diameter) belong at the top level of the part JSON. EDIT these values to match your supplier and company standards. The file must remain valid JSON (limit values are expressions).

rules.message: Drilled-hole depth exceeds 5× diameter: deep-hole drilling may be required, increasing cost.
Drilled-hole depth exceeds 3× diameter: the drill may wander or break, and chip evacuation becomes difficult (DFMPro wording “diameter-to-depth ratio < 3” is interpreted here as depth/diameter).
The drill enters a surface that is not perpendicular to the hole axis (risk of drill wandering).
The drill exits through a surface that is not perpendicular to the hole axis (uneven breakout/burrs may result).
The blind-hole bottom is specified as flat: a standard drill leaves a conical bottom, which can cause problems for subsequent boring.
The hole intersects a cavity: the drill may wander when it re-enters the material.
Where the hole intersects a cavity, its axis lies inside the cavity (at minimum, the axis should remain outside the cavity).
Partial hole: less than 75% of the hole area is supported by material (risk of drill wandering).
Non-standard hole size: a special tool may be required, increasing manufacturing and inventory costs.
Deep pocket: depth exceeds 4× tool diameter (tool diameter ≈ 2× corner radius); long tools may deflect, break, or vibrate.
Sharp internal corner: cannot be produced by conventional milling; use EDM or revise the geometry.
The narrow region between features is smaller than the minimum permitted cutter diameter (min_tool_diameter).
Non-standard side or bottom radius (use one standard side radius and one standard bottom radius).
Side and bottom surfaces are not perpendicular: multi-axis machining may be required, increasing cost.
The feature is not accessible to the tool in the intended machining orientation.
Tool relief in the blind-turned bore is less than 3% of the bore diameter.
The end of the keyway is not rounded to match the cutter (radius = half the width because cutter diameter = keyway width; inferred from the DFMPro description).
Length / minimum diameter exceeds 8: a tailstock or steady rest may be required to prevent part deflection.
Sharp internal corner in turning: a larger radius is needed to accommodate the tool nose radius.
Contour angle exceeds 58° from the axis: it cannot be machined in a single turning operation (steep or wall-parallel grooves).
Axial slot is not symmetric about the rotation axis: likely a modelling error that may cause assembly problems.
